resources.string: Create a course in Courses by entering a name and category. Topics and a schedule are optional and can be configured later. Up to 10 unfinished courses can have their own colors.

Type a category or choose a suggestion. A new category is created when you save the course. The trash icon deletes a category independently of the form: canceling the form does not undo this deletion. Courses remain without a category.

Edit list opens unfinished topics as text, one per line. Paste, reorder or remove lines and choose Apply. Cancel keeps the previous list. Completed topics remain outside the editor; matching names block applying and show the conflicting line numbers.

Hold a saved topic to mark it complete. Hold it again to remove the mark. A short tap does nothing; scrolling cancels the gesture. Save pending list edits before using this gesture. Manual topic marks never create calendar sessions.

Choose Configure in an unfinished course to set weekdays and start times. End times and the final date are optional. Equal times mean zero minutes; an earlier end means the next day. Configuring a paused course resumes sessions. Topics are not assigned to dates.

The Sessions screen shows today\'s and yesterday\'s sessions. After the end time, or 90 minutes after the start if no end was set, an unanswered session asks whether you studied. Choose Done and select the topics you actually finished, in any order. You may also save Done with no finished topics. Skipped does not change topic progress.

Choose a date in Calendar to view session results. Today’s and yesterday’s sessions can be changed. Bright stripes mean Done; pale stripes mean Planned or Skipped, with a cross for skipped sessions. Past unanswered sessions become Skipped on the next day. Courses without topics count completed sessions instead of showing a percentage.

Calendar history retention is shared by all courses. The default keeps today and the previous 365 local calendar days; you can choose 1–3650 days or turn cleanup off. A session on the boundary remains, and only earlier local dates are removed. Shortening the period requires confirmation because the next cleanup will remove more old records.

A completion offer appears when marking a session that completes the final topic. The course shows All topics completed. New sessions stop until incomplete topics are added. Pause keeps history and the color. Completing marks remaining topics complete, releases the color and prevents editing. Start again permanently clears all topic progress and previous sessions, assigns the first free color, and leaves the schedule empty. Deleting permanently removes the course and its history.

Enable reminders in Settings and allow Android notifications. If Android requests permission for alarms and reminders, allow it for reminders at the exact start and end time. A session without an end time gets the result reminder 90 minutes after it starts. Tap it to mark the result. Declining permission does not block the tracker.

Create a manual backup in Settings and choose where to save the file. Weekly backup can independently create new files in a permanently selected folder about once a week; Android does not guarantee an exact time, and the storage provider must remain available. Existing successful files are not deleted automatically. The copy contains courses, topics, schedules, session history, and the selected language. To restore, choose any manual or weekly backup and confirm the full replacement after it is checked. Backups cannot be merged. Canceling or choosing an invalid file does not change current data. Keep files private: this version does not encrypt them. A saved folder is device-specific and must be chosen again on a new phone.
